title: Access modifiers and polymorphic overriding
answer: Yes, access modifiers constrain whether an override is legal and where callers can use the method. An overriding method may keep or widen the parent's accessibility but cannot reduce it. Once a valid override is accessible to the caller, runtime dispatch still selects the implementation based on the runtime object. Access control is checked against the compile-time context, while overriding determines the executed instance implementation. This preserves the parent's callable contract.
